fields.evidence: Ran `npx vitest run tests/test_reconciliation_outgoing_messages.workers.test.ts -t test_UAT_AC2281` — fails at line 233: expected payload.html to be the rendered invite body, received undefined. apps/control-app/src/mail.ts:200 submits `text: message.body` to Resend (doc comment at lines 52-53: 'the Resend adapter sends it as `text`'). Story story-7d255580's Reconciliation Decisions flag this as a CODE-ISSUE: REQ-197 (later intent, governs) requires the body to be HTML; AC acceptance_criterion-a9a7dbf2 captures that intent. The test correctly encodes the AC; only a production change can make it pass.
fields.proposed_change: apps/control-app/src/mail.ts line 200: change `text: message.body,` to `html: message.body,` and update the doc comment at lines 52-53 to state the body is a single HTML part sent as Resend's `html` field. No test, AC or story changes needed.

items.hypothesis: resendMailer at apps/control-app/src/mail.ts:200 submits the body as Resend text (REQ-196 shape) while REQ-197, the later in-scope intent, decided the body is HTML in one part; the adapter must send html: message.body and the FC_REQ-196 exact-payload assertion pinning text is superseded.
items.instructions: Root cause confirmed by the iteration-1 builder: apps/control-app/src/mail.ts:200 sends `text: message.body`, so the provider never receives `html` and AC-2281 fails. REQ-197 (request-704fe21e.md:123, later than REQ-196) decides "The body is HTML, and it is one part", and REQ-196 itself prescribed this as one line in the adapter. code_frozen is lifted for mail.ts in this batch: change the Resend payload to carry the body as `html` (one part only; do NOT add a derived text part or port textFrom, because multipart is REQ-205 and out of scope), and correct the Message.body doc comment (~lines 52-53) that says the adapter sends it as text. The exact-shape assertion in test_UAT_FC_REQ-196_resend_adapter_sends_and_returns_the_provider_message_id expects `text: ...`; REQ-197 supersedes that, so rewrite only that field expectation to `html:`, keeping the rest of the exact payload/endpoint/bearer/id checks. All mail.ts consumer tests (FC_REQ-196 suite, AC2275-2278, AC2286) must stay green.

items.instructions: The production gates already behave as AC-2257 claims: ownsBusiness reads role === owner (identity.ts:1232), canInvite, invite, record and status are gated on it, and the admin route is gated on ownsPlatformBusiness. The test was added today and has never passed because its fixture is incomplete. aCustomerOwner() and the staff member are platform-tenant users with memberships only, so owner.businessId holds no users rows. GET /api/people returns [] for both callers, the list-equality check is vacuous, and ownerPeople.people[0] is undefined. Fix the evidence, not the code: before the list comparison, have the owner put a real contact into owner.businessId through the product path (postInvite with the owner token, as the AC-2249 test above does). Assert both lists are non-empty and contain that contact, then use it as the target for the record and status refusals. Strengthen those two refusals by reading the target back and asserting its display name and status are unchanged. Keep every existing assertion, including the 403s, the canInvite difference, the admin 404 for staff and the 400 for the operator. Do not change production code.

ladder.rung1: REQ-194 requires that no permission check reads role beyond the owner question, which is exactly what the test asserts. No later intent in scope contradicts it.
ladder.rung2: At the reference, invite, record and status are gated on ownsBusiness and the admin route on ownsPlatformBusiness, both reading role === owner only (identity.ts:1232-1238, router.ts:1284-1299, 1450-1452, 1489-1491, 1563-1565). The code already matches the test intent.
ladder.rung3: Decided here: the assertions stand and the fixture is fixed. The test seeds no contact in the business it lists, so it changes and the code does not. No override.

- The committed `MODULE_CLIENT_JS` in `packages/framework/src/modules/module-assets.ts` has that scoping: contact-form, carousel, account-portal and account-chrome each sit in their own `{ … }` block.

- `node --check` on the bundle extracted from `MODULE_CLIENT_JS` passes, so the duplicate-`const` SyntaxError behind the 4 page-error violations is gone.

items.hypothesis: tests/reconciliation-assistant-looking-surface-worker.workers.test.ts calls route(request, env, deps) with three args, so the deps object lands in route's scope parameter (router.ts:1075-1081), scope.businessId is undefined, and /api/ai/session throws a 500.
items.instructions: Both failures are 500s on the first /api/ai/session call at lines 164 and 232, caused by the test, not the product. The local chat helpers at lines 161 and 228 call route(request(path, body), env, deps), but route's signature is route(request, env, scope, deps, ctx), so the deps object is read as the scope and real deps default to {}. Fix the test so it passes a real scope as the third argument and the deps as the fourth: route(request(path, body), env, { businessId: TENANT }, { launch: browser.launch }) for AC2025, and route(request(path, body), blind, { businessId: TENANT }, {}) for AC2024. TENANT ('looking') is the business the Worker's dev-open scope resolves to (scope.ts: businessId = env.TENANT_ID), and it is the one the test seeds through worker.fetch and reads back through forTenant(TENANT). Leave every assertion as it is. Production code is frozen and already matches the reference (sessionFidelity, and chatHost(env, requireScope(), deps, url.origin)). If AC2025 then fails further in, report the actual returned values rather than adjusting assertions. The orphan AC-2025 clears when its UAT passes. Run the sibling business Worker tests to confirm they stay green.

(1) AC2109, session-texts.test.ts:232: the test asserts toContain(DOC-33), but AC-2109 now forbids any DOC-<n> id in the reminder. Replace it with what the AC verifies: the reminder points to the knowledge base for the method (/knowledge base/), matches no /DOC-\d+/, has no unfilled {placeholder} and does not end with a separator. Make these assertions on what the model received (firstSaw), not only on consultantReminder(). Rename the test so it no longer says doc33, keeping the test_UAT_AC2109_ token. (2) AC2066, consultant-role.test.ts:200-210: the slice ends at the first newline, so it captures only the site line. AC-2109 makes the reminder six paragraphs separated by blank lines, and the word client first appears in paragraph 2. Capture the whole reminder block as sent: from the site-line opening through the method entry (priming.json:273-298 in the working tree), or the end of the message text that carries it. Assert client, no user and no legacy name over that block, and fix the stale one-line comment. Do not loosen the user or legacy checks. (3) AC1409, deployed.workers.test.ts:610-713: run it and read the first failing assertion. The working tree stores transcripts as chat tickets with chat_transcript comments (ai.ts:27-31, tickets.ts:388) and audit records at audit/<tenant>/<session>/ (ai.ts:284), as the AC says. If the failure is test drift against the working-tree API (helper, route shape, seed), fix the test so it still proves every observation AC-1409 lists. If production contradicts AC-1409, report blocked_by code_frozen with the failing assertion and the file:line; do not edit production.

fields.evidence: Ran `npx vitest run tests/reconciliation-consultant-image-generation.workers.test.ts -t AC2380`: 1 failed. The unsupported-shape tool result reads 'Error: CreateImage failed (unknown_aspect_ratio). That is not a shape this generator offers. The host reports: Backend "openai" does not support "aspectRatios": 21:9 is not among 1:1, 3:2, 2:3', so the assertion that no tool result contains 'openai' fails. REQ-208 ('no error sentence or line of the manual names one'), the property-1 header comment in apps/control-app/src/imagegen.ts, and AC-2380 (which lists the unsupported-shape path explicitly) all require this text to be free of vendor names. The test is correct; the code leaks the vendor name in this one path.
fields.proposed_change: apps/control-app/src/imagegen.ts: where imageSurface() builds the plugin via images.createImagePlugin(...), wrap the create_image tool's result/error text so any vendor identity is scrubbed before it reaches the model. Either drop the framework's 'The host reports: …' detail from errors, or replace every occurrence of IMAGE_PROVIDER (and the backend's model id) with a neutral word such as 'the generator', keeping the 'not a shape this generator offers' sentence and the list of supported ratios. A cleaner alternative is to fix it upstream in the framework imagegen plugin by not interpolating the backend name into the unknown_aspect_ratio error, then regenerate apps/control-app/src/generated/ai-imagegen.js. No test or AC change is needed; test_UAT_AC2380 passes once the text is vendor-free.

items.instructions: AC-1400's UAT (tests/reconciliation-workspace-build-artifacts.test.ts) is valid evidence. It fails because other suites rebuild the shared apps/control-app/dist-assets tree while it is reading that tree. The writers are reconciliation-1c-launcher-bootstrap, reconciliation-platform-asset-tree-swap, reconciliation-marked-points-served-modules, test_UAT_FC_BUG-71_framework_import_graph, reconciliation-product-ticket-store-schema and reconciliation-builder-workspace-import-graph, each via run(['assets']) or buildControlAppAssets(REPO). The build renames dist-assets to dist-assets.retired, then renames dist-assets.staging into place, and every run shares one .staging folder. So a concurrent reader sees no tree (503 'not built' / 404) or a half-written one, and two concurrent builds clear each other's staging (the ENOTEMPTY reported in REPORT-11524). Establish mutual exclusion over that tree across Vitest workers, in test infrastructure only. Every suite-initiated `1c assets` build holds one exclusive cross-process lock for its whole duration. AC-1400's UAT holds the same lock across its reads of the served tree. Reuse the mkdir-lock pattern already in tests/support/local-d1.ts (withLock, ~lines 104-128) by lifting it into a shared tests/support helper with an async form; do not write a second lock mechanism. Its stale threshold must exceed the longest holder (AC-1400 runs up to 120 s; the current 120 s stale limit would let a waiter break a live lock). Do not change tools/generate/src/cli/assets.ts, builder.ts or any production file, and do not change AC-1400's assertions. The dependency suites must stay green with the lock in place.

No test or AC changes.

- **AC-2486 test:** it checks that the SVG caption says this. The old caption failed it.
